#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Lazy DRAFT create for the release train's asset-upload steps (gh-1801).
#
# The train workflows (ci.yml binaries/web-spa, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli/build-extension) need a release object to attach assets
# to, but the release must never go live from an upload step: `fa update`
# resolves the `latest` release and hard-fails without the SIGNED
# SHA256SUMS(.sig) (bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate), which only the
# tag-run release-provenance job can upload. This script creates the
# release as a DRAFT — nothing else:
#
#   - body = scripts/release_notes.sh output (curated `## <version>`
#     CHANGELOG section → curated `## Unreleased` → conventional commits;
#     the gh-1172 curated-notes contract), with a minimal fallback —
#     never `--generate-notes` (review threads 3/7);
#   - body carries `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job> -->`
#     so scripts/release_draft_guard.sh can reclaim the draft on failure
#     (review threads 4/8) — matrix legs override the identity via
#     RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. binaries-linux-x64) so a failed leg's
#     guard can never match a sibling's in-flight draft;
#   - the view→create race is tolerated (`|| true`): a sibling leg or the
#     attach path may create the release between our view and create —
#     the loser just uploads into the winner's release;
#   - it NEVER publishes and NEVER flags latest: the single publish point
#     of a tag train is release-provenance's "Upload provenance assets"
#     step (`gh release edit --draft=false --latest` after SHA256SUMS.sig
#     lands). A red provenance leaves the previous release as latest —
#     safe degradation, never a provenance-less latest (v1.0.630 window).
#
# Usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (optional leg-suffixed override),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}}"

# The guard greps exactly this class — validate here so a malformed
# override fails loud instead of stamping a marker the guard could never
# match (a forever-orphaned draft).
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the draft lifecycle guard could never reclaim such a draft" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Already created (by a sibling leg, the attach path, or a previous run)?
# Drafts and published releases both resolve here — upload-only is safe.
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "release $tag already exists — lazy draft create skipped"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: curated notes (CHANGELOG section / Unreleased / conventional
# commits) plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
# stderr is NOT swallowed: release_notes.sh's ::error gates (e.g. the
# duplicate-'## Unreleased' curation guard) must stay visible even when
# the minimal fallback below keeps the train moving.
notes_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-lazy-notes.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$notes_file"' EXIT
if ! bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes.sh" "$tag" >"$notes_file" ||
  [ ! -s "$notes_file" ]; then
  printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" >"$notes_file"
fi
marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: $identity -->"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes_file" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >>"$notes_file"

# DRAFT-first (gh-1801): a create here must never publish — the resolved
# asset list at this point can never include the signed checksums. The
# race-lost create is tolerated (the winner owns the release).
gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes_file" || true
echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release draft lifecycle guard (issue #282): a run that creates a release
# draft must end with it published or deleted — never orphan it. `gh
# release create <tag> <assets...>` uploads the assets through a DRAFT
# first and publishes only after every upload succeeds; a step dying
# mid-upload (the v0.1.190 rot) leaves that draft behind forever.
#
# Usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>
#
# OWNERSHIP-SCOPED DELETE (review of #294): the guard deletes ONLY the
# draft this very run+job created. daily-publish runs the macOS and
# mobile legs concurrently against the same derived tag; a failed leg's
# guard firing on the SIBLING leg's mid-upload draft would destroy a
# healthy concurrent release. Draft-capable creates
# (scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh, scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh)
# stamp the draft body with
#   <!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job_id> -->
# and the guard deletes only on an exact match against GITHUB_RUN_ID /
# GITHUB_JOB (both GitHub Actions default env). Matrix jobs share
# GITHUB_JOB across legs (ci.yml binaries, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli) — those steps stamp a LEG-SUFFIXED identity via
# RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. run/123/job/binaries-linux-x64) and the
# guard step must export the same value, so a failed leg can never match
# a sibling's in-flight draft. A foreign or unmarked draft is NEVER
# deleted here — the daily sweeper
# (scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh) reclaims genuinely orphaned drafts
# after 24h.
#
# Called from workflow steps with `if: always() && job.status != 'success'`
# so it runs on failure AND cancellation. A published release or a missing
# release is a no-op; a draft for <tag> is deleted (its assets are
# unpublished by definition — published releases are the artifact store,
# issue #282 E2). The tag itself is never touched.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
: "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}"
: "${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/job/$GITHUB_JOB}"
# Validate (mirror of release_lazy_draft.sh): an unmatchable identity
# would silently orphan the draft forever.
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the marker could never be stamped or matched" >&2
  exit 1
}

state=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft 2>/dev/null || echo missing)
if [ "$state" != "true" ]; then
  echo "release lifecycle guard: $tag is ${state} (published or absent) — nothing to clean"
  exit 0
fi

notes=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json body --jq '.body // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
owner=$(printf '%s' "$notes" \
  | grep -oE 'release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+' \
  | head -1 | sed 's/^release-draft-owner: //' || true)

if [ "$owner" != "$identity" ]; then
  echo "::warning::release lifecycle guard: draft $tag is owned by '${owner:-<unmarked>}' (we are $identity) — refusing to delete a draft this run+job did not create; a sibling leg may be mid-upload. The daily sweeper reclaims orphaned drafts after 24h (issue #282)."
  exit 0
fi

gh release delete "$tag" --repo "$repo" --yes
echo "::warning::release lifecycle guard: deleted own draft $tag — the run failed after creating it; a draft must be published or deleted, never orphaned (issue #282)"

- run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # gh-1522: the bundle version rides the TAG (GITHUB_REF_NAME), not
          # the committed placeholder pubspec.
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          # dart build cli produces: <output>/bundle/{bin/fah, lib/*.dylib}
          # We rename the executable to `fa`, write version.txt, then archive
          # the whole bundle so the installer can extract bin/ + lib/ together.
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$version" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      # gh-1280 NG2: «compiles» is not «works» — every release arch boots its
      # binary before the asset is archived/uploaded (same smoke as
      # binaries-pr). The usage marker (cli_help.dart "USAGE") discriminates
      # the real CLI help from a binary that merely prints something.
      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          grep -qi "usage" <<<"$out" || { echo "fa --help did not print usage"; exit 1; }

      - name: Archive bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          archive_name="fa-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}"
          if [ "${{ matrix.archive }}" = "zip" ]; then
            asset="${archive_name}.zip"
            cd build/out && 7z a -tzip "../../$asset" bundle && cd -
          else
            asset="${archive_name}.tar.gz"
            tar -czf "$asset" -C build/out bundle
          fi
          ls -lh "$asset"

      - name: Upload archive to GitHub Release
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Matrix legs share GITHUB_JOB=binaries — the leg-suffixed draft
          # owner identity keeps the failure-path guard scoped to the leg
          # that created the draft, never a sibling's mid-upload one.
          RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY: run/${{ github.run_id }}/job/${{ github.job }}-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}

# mirrors web-spa (additive attach, quality-gate keyed) because the
  # failure mode it kills is identical in shape: the extension's former
  # ONLY producer was build-macos.yml build-extension, a once-daily leg
  # deriving "latest+1 at its own dispatch moment" — any v* tag train
  # landing after the daily leg published a draft WITHOUT fa-extension.zip
  # and the gh-1832 required-assets gate correctly stranded it
  # (v1.0.637/v1.0.638 stuck, 2026-10-24; the manual recovery dispatch
  # from memory note n_1012 risked becoming the operating mode). With the
  # train producing the zip, the gate's precondition is met by the train
  # no matter when the daily leg ran; the daily leg keeps pre-staging the
  # next-tag draft and stays the n_1012 emergency producer.
  build-extension:
    name: Build Chrome extension (release)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # Additive REQUIRED asset, same semantics as web-spa: an SDK flake or
    # vendor-fetch hiccup must NOT hold CLI provenance hostage — the
    # release-provenance required-assets gate (gh-1832) is the single
    # publish blocker and strands the draft loudly on the MISSING asset
    # (previous release stays latest). continue-on-error keeps the check
    # green; the failed steps stay visible on the run page.
    continue-on-error: true
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach fa-extension.zip to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Blobless full history: the lazy draft create (gh-1801 rework)
          # builds the release body via scripts/release_notes.sh — same
          # reason as the web-spa job's checkout (gh-1477).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      # gh-1684 decision 4 + #1431 exact-patch pin: the SAME pinned SDK
      # every other fa-extension.zip leg carries (extension-size-gate,
      # build-macos.yml build-extension) — the rev normalization absorbs
      # canvaskit/skwasm churn, the pin keeps every build comparable.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.7'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      # browser_ext/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root), so
      # its pub get must follow the root's — same as the PR-time
      # extension-size-gate leg and build-macos.yml build-extension.
      - name: dart pub get (root + browser_ext/dart)
        run: |
          dart pub get
          cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get

      # Full artifact: SW agent (dart2js) + the Flutter panel app embedded,
      # exactly what the landing page's releases/latest/download link
      # serves. Identical invocation as the PR-time gate leg (gh-1684 AC3)
      # and the build-macos.yml release leg.
      - name: Build extension zip
        run: bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app

      # AC1 (#1096) + gh-1684 AC5: one baseline, one enforcement rule — the
      # IDENTICAL invocation the extension-size-gate PR leg and the
      # build-macos.yml release leg run, gate BEFORE upload (a budget
      # regression must not reach the release assets). Baseline is
      # committed — no --init-if-missing here.
      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (fa-extension.zip)
        run: python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv

      # gh-1801 (rework): DRAFT-first, NEVER publish here. fa-extension.zip
      # is a gh-1832 REQUIRED asset, but even a complete asset set must not
      # go live without the SIGNED SHA256SUMS — only the tag-run
      # release-provenance job owns the --draft=false --latest flip. Create
      # the draft with the curated notes + the draft-owner marker and
      # upload; --clobber keeps the stable asset name pointing at the
      # newest build. No guard step ON PURPOSE (same reasoning as web-spa):
      # this job is continue-on-error — on failure the train (binaries →
      # provenance) CONTINUES and must find the draft alive; a genuinely
      # orphaned draft is reclaimed by the 24h sweeper.
      - name: Upload extension to the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          asset="fa-extension.zip"
          cp build/fa-extension.zip "$asset"
          ls -lh "$asset"
          bash scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" "$asset" --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

      # Mirror of the web-spa summary flag: surface the miss in the run's
      # step summary (covers build/size-gate/upload flakes); the failed
      # steps remain visible in the job view. The release-provenance
      # required-assets gate is what actually blocks the publish.
      - name: Flag missing extension in step summary
        if: failure()
        run: |
          {
            echo '## fa-extension.zip NOT shipped this release'
            echo ''
            echo 'The extension build job failed (continue-on-error: the gh-1832 gate strands the release without it). See the failed steps above.'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # SEC-07 (#795): the installer's default trust path is SIGNED checksums.
  # This job aggregates every fa-* asset of the release into SHA256SUMS and
  # signs it with the FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY repo secret (openssl RSA —
  # already available on runners, no new dependency). The signing key is a
  # channel separate from the release assets, so a checksum file served from
  # the same compromised source as the binary cannot vouch for itself.
  # Fail-closed: without the secret the release publishes NO provenance and
  # this job goes red — install.sh aborts with E_PROVENANCE_MISSING on it.
  # Needs web-spa (#1100, continue-on-error) and build-extension
  # (gh-1847, continue-on-error) for ordering only: the web bundle and
  # the extension zip cannot hold CLI provenance hostage. The ordering
  # makes the fa-* sweep deterministic — web-spa/extension success ->
  # zip signed, failure -> zip absent — never a half-updated manifest,
  # and the gh-1832 gate below never races a slow attach.
  release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa, build-extension]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      # gh-1832: PUBLISH-BLOCKING required-assets gate. The single source of
      # truth is scripts/release_required_assets.txt, consumed by
      # scripts/assert_release_assets.sh. v1.0.635 published without
      # fa-extension.zip because the extension's only producer (the daily
      # build-macos.yml build-extension leg) attached it to a "latest+1"
      # draft while this train published the tagged release — every leg
      # green, nothing asserted the published set. A missing asset here
      # fails the release run loudly and leaves the release a DRAFT (the
      # previous release stays latest) instead of publishing a partial one.
      - name: Assert required release assets (gh-1832 gate)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |
            sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > embedded-anchor.pem
          openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded-anchor.pem -noout ||
            { echo "::error::site/install.sh trust anchor does not parse as a public key — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"; exit 1; }
          cmp embedded-anchor.pem pub.pem ||
            { echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY drifted from the trust anchor embedded in site/install.sh — rotate the keypair: update install.signing_public_key in site/install-config.yaml, regenerate installers, and update the repo secret TOGETHER. Refusing to sign (fail-closed)."; exit 1; }
          rm -f pub.pem embedded-anchor.pem

      - name: Upload provenance assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          # gh-1801 (rework): THE publish point of the train. The release
          # now carries every fa-* asset AND the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) —
          # the first moment `fa update` can actually serve it (it
          # hard-fails without the signed checksums, bin/self_manage.dart).
          # Flip draft=false + latest here and ONLY here: a red provenance
          # leaves the previous release as latest (safe degradation)
          # instead of stranding a provenance-less one (the v1.0.630
          # empty/partial-latest window class).
          gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

      # gh-1899: the flip above publishes exactly ONE release object, but
      # GitHub does not atomically enforce one release per tag — two train
      # legs racing the lazy draft create can BOTH succeed (v1.0.641, run
      # 40163369302: twin drafts 87 ms apart), and the unpicked twin then
      # rots until the 24h sweeper deletes it and files a recurring sweep
      # issue. The tag is published and servable now: reclaim this run's
      # twin drafts. Success-path only — a red provenance keeps the draft
      # as the rerun --failed recovery vessel.
      # Best-effort by design (gh-1899 review): the flip above already
      # published the release — a cleanup-only API blip here must NOT fail
      # the provenance job (release-asset-smoke gates on its result and
      # would silently skip for a release that is actually fine). Warn
      # and stay green; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop.
      - name: Reclaim orphaned draft twins (gh-1899)
        if: success()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_dedupe.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"

  # gh-1832 AC3: post-publish smoke. Probes (1) EVERY releases/(latest/)?
  # download/ URL the fa1.dev landing page exposes (site/index.html) and
  # (2) the full required set from scripts/release_required_assets.txt via
  # a 1-byte ranged GET each — red on anything but HTTP 200/206. Rides the
  # tag train only (PR runs never probe release URLs); a 404 here is the
  # owner-facing v1.0.635 symptom caught the same hour it appears.
  release-asset-smoke:

      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||

steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Full history: release_notes.sh falls back to "commits since the
          # previous tag" when the CHANGELOG has no section for this version.
          # gh-1477: blobless — the notes read commit MESSAGES, never
          # historical file blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Download DMG artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          path: dmgs
          pattern: Fa-macos-*
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: List downloaded artifacts
        run: ls -laR dmgs/

      - name: Merge macOS auto-update manifest
        run: |
          python3 -m pip install --user pyyaml
          chmod +x scripts/merge-mac-update-manifest.sh
          scripts/merge-mac-update-manifest.sh dmgs dmgs/latest-mac.yml
          cat dmgs/latest-mac.yml

      - name: Create or update GitHub Release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # PAT (not the job token) so the tag push fires tag CI — the
          # attach-or-create script builds its push URL only when GH_TOKEN
          # is set; without it `git push ""` died with "fatal: bad
          # repository ''" (2026-10-22 v1.0.626 mobile leg).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          DMGS=$(ls dmgs/*.dmg 2>/dev/null || true)
          ZIPS=$(ls dmgs/*-mac.zip 2>/dev/null || true)
          MANIFEST="dmgs/latest-mac.yml"
          echo "DMGs to upload: $DMGS"
          echo "ZIPs to upload: $ZIPS"

          STABLE_COPIES=()
          for zip in $ZIPS; do
            base=$(basename "$zip")
            # Skip no-sandbox zips from the auto-update stable names; the
            # sandboxed build is the default update feed.
            if [[ "$base" == *nosandbox* ]]; then
              continue
            fi
            if [[ "$base" == *arm64* ]]; then
              cp "$zip" "dmgs/fa-macos-arm64-mac.zip"
              STABLE_COPIES+=("dmgs/fa-macos-arm64-mac.zip")
            elif [[ "$base" == *x86_64* ]]; then
              cp "$zip" "dmgs/fa-macos-x64-mac.zip"
              STABLE_COPIES+=("dmgs/fa-macos-x64-mac.zip")
            fi
          done

          # Extract the raw binary from the .app bundle and upload it as the
          # plain asset name (fa-macos-arm64 / fa-macos-x64) so `fa update`
          # and direct downloads work without knowing the version suffix.
          for zip in $ZIPS; do
            base=$(basename "$zip")
            if [[ "$base" == *nosandbox* ]]; then
              continue
            fi
            unzip -qo "$zip" -d /tmp/fa-extract >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            BIN="/tmp/fa-extract/Fa.app/Contents/MacOS/Fa"
            if [ -f "$BIN" ]; then
              if [[ "$base" == *arm64* ]]; then
                cp "$BIN" "dmgs/fa-macos-arm64"
                ASSETS+=("dmgs/fa-macos-arm64")
              elif [[ "$base" == *x86_64* ]]; then
                cp "$BIN" "dmgs/fa-macos-x64"
                ASSETS+=("dmgs/fa-macos-x64")
              fi
              chmod +x "dmgs/fa-macos-arm64" "dmgs/fa-macos-x64" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
            rm -rf /tmp/fa-extract
          done
          ASSETS=($DMGS $ZIPS $MANIFEST "${STABLE_COPIES[@]}")

          # Notes come from the CHANGELOG section for this version, with a
          # conventional-commit fallback (issue #282: no more filler
          # bodies); the install hints stay as a footer.
          bash scripts/release_notes.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" > release-notes.md || true
          printf '\n## Installation\n- **macOS**: Download the DMG for your architecture (`arm64` for Apple Silicon, `x86_64` for Intel) and drag Fa.app to Applications. In-app updates use the ZIP + latest-mac.yml feed.\n- **Linux**: Download tar.gz, extract and run the `bundle/fa` binary.\n- **Windows**: Download zip, extract and run the `fa.exe`.\n' >> release-notes.md

          # Attach-or-create (issue #282 E3 + review of #294): idempotent
          # against the view->create race - a lost race uploads into the
          # winner's release instead of failing - and the create stamps an
          # ownership marker into the draft body, so the guard step below
          # only ever deletes THIS job's draft, never the mobile leg's
          # mid-upload draft on the same derived tag.
          bash scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" "${ASSETS[@]}"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): the create above uploads
      # assets through a draft — a failed/cancelled run must delete it,
      # never orphan it (the v0.1.190 rot). Ownership-scoped (review of
      # #294): the guard deletes only a draft whose body carries THIS
      # run+job's marker — a sibling leg's draft is never touched.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: always() && job.status != 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Attach assets to <tag>'s release, creating it when missing — the single
# draft-capable create path for build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# (issue #282 E3 + review of #294).
#
# Race-idempotent (E3): if `gh release create` loses the view→create race
# (another job/run created the release in between), fall back to
# uploading into the winner's release instead of failing. A failed create
# would fire the job's draft lifecycle guard against the WINNER's
# in-flight draft.
#
# Ownership-stamped: the create path makes a DRAFT (gh-1801 rework: the
# release never goes live from a leg — the tag-run release-provenance job
# publishes + flags latest once the signed SHA256SUMS is attached). The
# body stamps
#   <!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job_id> -->
# and release_draft_guard.sh deletes that draft ONLY on an exact
# run+job match — never the sibling leg's mid-upload draft (daily-publish
# runs the mobile and macOS legs concurrently on the same derived tag).
# The marker is an invisible HTML comment in the body.
#
# Usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <asset> [<asset>...]
#   reads the release body from release-notes.md in the CWD (a minimal
#   body is written when the file is missing/empty)
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <assets...>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
shift
assets=("$@")
if [ "${#assets[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  # gh-1801 hard refusal: creating a release with zero resolved assets is
  # the `fa update` breaker (an empty `latest` 404s every
  # fa-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz until backfill — v1.0.630, 2026-10-23). Attaching
  # is the caller's only honest option when it resolved nothing — fail
  # loud here, never create empty. Pinned by
  # test/release_empty_latest_guard_test.dart.
  echo "::error::no assets to attach for $tag — refusing to create or touch a release with an empty asset list (gh-1801): resolve at least one artifact or skip the release step" >&2
  exit 1
fi

upload_all() { # exists-path: upload + (servable-only) publish + latest
  for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
    gh release upload "$tag" "$asset" --clobber --repo "$repo"
  done
  # Latest policy (#282 + gh-1801 rework): publish + latest ONLY when the
  # release can actually serve `fa update` — that means the signed
  # checksums are already on it (`fa update` hard-fails without
  # SHA256SUMS(.sig), bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate). A release
  # carrying them but still draft means provenance ran and its own flip
  # failed — recover it here. Any other case stays draft/unflipped: the
  # tag-run release-provenance job (ci.yml) is the single owner of the
  # --draft=false --latest flip, and a red provenance must leave the
  # PREVIOUS release as latest instead of stranding a provenance-less one
  # (the v1.0.630 incident window).
  if release_serves_fa_update; then
    gh release edit "$tag" --draft=false --latest --repo "$repo"
    # gh-1899: same duplicate-tag race as the tag train — a twin draft
    # minted by a sibling leg of THIS run would otherwise rot until the
    # 24h sweeper. The tag is published and servable here (the flip is
    # gated on the signed checksums), so own-run twin drafts are orphans.
    bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_draft_dedupe.sh" "$tag" \
      || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the release is published and servable, so this is cleanup noise only; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"
  else
    echo "release $tag is not yet servable (no SHA256SUMS on it) — publish+latest left to the release-provenance step (gh-1801)"
  fi
}

# fa-update servability = the signed checksums are on the release. Every
# fa-* archive alone is NOT enough: `fa update` fetches SHA256SUMS(.sig)
# and aborts when either is missing (bin/self_manage.dart).
release_serves_fa_update() {
  local names
  names=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json assets --jq '.assets[].name' 2>/dev/null || true)
  printf '%s\n' "$names" | grep -qE '^SHA256SUMS(\.sig)?$'
}

if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  upload_all
  echo "✅ attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) to existing release $tag"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: prepared notes (CHANGELOG section / conventional-commit fallback)
# plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
notes="release-notes.md"
marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)} -->"
[ -s "$notes" ] || printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" > "$notes"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >> "$notes"

# A `gh release create` for a MISSING tag mints a lightweight API tag:
# no push event → no ci.yml tag run → no publish/binaries (the v0.1.408
# silent class, issue #597). If the ref is absent, create it as an
# ANNOTATED tag and push it with the PAT the job already carries
# (GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT in build-macos) so the tag CI fires. A push with
# the workflow's default github.token would be equally dead — GitHub
# suppresses events triggered by GITHUB_TOKEN.
# Gate on the DEFINITE missing verdict (ls-remote --exit-code rc 2):
# sandboxes without an origin remote fatal with 128 — indeterminable
# falls through to the plain create path (test fixtures rely on it).
set +e
git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1
ls_remote_rc=$?
set -e
if [ "$ls_remote_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  # Fail fast BEFORE the cryptic crash: the push URL below collapses to ''
  # when GH_TOKEN is unset, and git's `fatal: bad repository ''` does not
  # point at the env gap (run 39766453580, v1.0.626 mobile leg). Callers
  # must export GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT (or a job-scoped App token) — the
  # workflow GITHUB_TOKEN is not a substitute (GitHub suppresses events it
  # triggers, so the tag CI would never fire).
  if [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    echo "::error::tag $tag is missing but GH_TOKEN is not set — the annotated-tag push would run 'git push \"\"'. Set GH_TOKEN (PAT/App token) on the calling step, or the tag can never be minted here." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  target="${RELEASE_TARGET_SHA:-${GITHUB_SHA:?}}"
  echo "tag $tag missing — creating annotated tag at $target (PAT push, fires tag CI)"
  git fetch origin "$target" --depth=1 2>/dev/null || git fetch origin main --depth=50
  # CI checkout carries no identity; annotate as the actions bot without
  # touching global config (empty ident → exit 128, run 35426119831).
  git -c user.name="github-actions[bot]" \
      -c user.email="41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com" \
      tag -a "$tag" -m "Release $tag" "$target"
  git push "${GH_TOKEN:+https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection-String-Password]@github.com/${repo}.git}" "refs/tags/$tag"
fi

# Bare vX.Y.Z title (#282): matches the tag, matches pub.dev. gh-1801
# rework: the create is DRAFT-ONLY. Whatever this leg resolved
# (AAB/IPA/store APKs, DMGs/zips) is not the signed provenance `fa update`
# demands — a leg that arrives first must never publish the release, let
# alone flag it latest (threads 2/6). The draft is ownership-stamped (the
# marker below) so this job's draft lifecycle guard reclaims it on
# failure; the tag-run binaries job attaches the CLI assets into it and

  release-mobile:
    name: Create Mobile GitHub Release
    needs: [version, build-android, build-android-apks, build-ios]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 15
    if: |
      always() &&
      ((needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android.result == 'skipped') ||
       (needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'skipped')) &&
      (needs.build-ios.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'skipped')
    permissions:

    steps:
      - name: Nothing to release
        # Both platforms picked a no-binary content mode (none /
        # metadata_only / screenshots_only) — nothing was built, so there

        with:

          path: artifacts/

      - name: Download Android AAB artifact
        if: needs.build-android.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: android-aab
          path: artifacts/

      - name: Download store APK artifact
        if: needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: android-apk-store
          path: artifacts/

      - name: Download god APK artifact
        if: needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: android-apk-god
          path: artifacts/

      - name: List downloaded artifacts
        if: needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
        run: ls -laR artifacts/

      - name: Create or update GitHub Release
        if: needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # PAT (not the job token) so the tag push fires tag CI — the
          # attach-or-create script builds its push URL only when GH_TOKEN
          # is set; without it `git push ""` died with "fatal: bad
          # repository ''" (2026-10-22 v1.0.626 mobile leg).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          AAB=$(find artifacts -name "*.aab" -type f | head -1)
          IPA=$(find artifacts -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          STORE_APK=$(find artifacts -name "app-store-release.apk" -type f | head -1)
          GOD_APK=$(find artifacts -name "app-god-release.apk" -type f | head -1)
          echo "AAB: $AAB"
          echo "IPA: $IPA"
          echo "store APK: $STORE_APK"
          echo "god APK: $GOD_APK"

          ASSETS=()
          [ -n "$AAB" ] && ASSETS+=("$AAB")
          [ -n "$IPA" ] && ASSETS+=("$IPA")
          [ -n "$STORE_APK" ] && ASSETS+=("$STORE_APK")
          [ -n "$GOD_APK" ] && ASSETS+=("$GOD_APK")

          # Notes come from the CHANGELOG section for this version, with a
          # conventional-commit fallback (issue #282: no more filler
          # bodies); the install hints stay as a footer.
          bash scripts/release_notes.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" > release-notes.md || true
          printf '\n## Installation\n- **Android**: Download the AAB and upload to Play Store, or use `flutter install`.\n- **Android god flavor (sideload only)**: install the god APK directly — see https://fa1.dev/android.\n- **iOS**: Download the IPA and upload to TestFlight via Xcode or Transporter.\n- **macOS**: Download the DMG from the macOS build workflow.\n' >> release-notes.md

          # Attach-or-create (issue #282 E3 + review of #294): idempotent
          # against the view->create race - a lost race uploads into the
          # winner's release instead of failing - and the create stamps an
          # ownership marker into the draft body, so the guard step below
          # only ever deletes THIS job's draft, never the macOS leg's
          # mid-upload draft on the same derived tag.
          bash scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" "${ASSETS[@]}"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): the create above uploads
      # assets through a draft — a failed/cancelled run must delete it,
      # never orphan it (the v0.1.190 rot). Ownership-scoped (review of
      # #294): the guard deletes only a draft whose body carries THIS
      # run+job's marker — a sibling leg's draft is never touched.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: >-
          always() && job.status != 'success' &&
          (needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'success')
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

content.text:
# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the quality gate is NOT re-run by
  # the release twin — the release-dedupe pre-check (gh-1625) short-circuits
  # every gate leg when the tag's GREEN push run already gates it, while
  # the release-specific legs (binaries attach, release-provenance,
  # installer-smoke) keep running on the twin (the retired comment here
  # only made the binaries UPLOAD idempotent — duplicate create +
  # --clobber, last wins — while the full 35-40 min gate still re-ran,
  # doubling release wall time).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays out — baselines are macOS-captured;
#                   the nightly build-release macOS row guards goldens on
#                   the pinned-font env, issue #1856 / #177 E5)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)

type: "note"
title: "Release-train recovery playbook — EMERGENCY FALLBACK after gh-1847 landed the systemic fix (gh-1845, 2026-10-24): when a v* tag run's \"Sign release checksums\" (release-provenance) fails with \"release <tag> is missing 1 required asset(s): fa-extension.zip — BLOCKING the publish\", the fix is NOT code: dispatch the producer with an explicit tag — `gh workflow run build-macos.yml --ref <tag> -f version=<tag> -f create_release=true` (its build-extension job is ubuntu-latest, fast, and adopts the existing draft via scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh) — wait for fa-extension.zip to appear on the release, then `gh run rerun <tag-run-id> --failed`. Root pattern: build-macos.yml build-extension derives \"latest+1 at its own dispatch moment\" and runs ~once daily, so any tag train landing after the daily leg has no fa-extension.zip and the gh-1832 gate correctly strands it as a draft (seen stuck: v1.0.637, v1.0.638 on 2026-10-24). \"Advance vpinned marker\" failing right after is downstream noise (pin_release.sh refuses to pin unsigned releases) — it self-heals once provenance lands. Note: gh run view --json jobs returns only the latest attempt; failed release-tail jobs may be absent from a stale ci-red ticket's job list if the report was filed before the tail finished. # Note: n_1012_9c1a

Release-train recovery playbook (gh-1845, 2026-10-24): when a v* tag run's "Sign release checksums" (release-provenance) fails with "release <tag> is missing 1 required asset(s): fa-extension.zip — BLOCKING the publish", the fix is NOT code: dispatch the producer with an explicit tag — `gh workflow run build-macos.yml --ref <tag> -f version=<tag> -f create_release=true` (its build-extension job is ubuntu-latest, fast, and adopts the existing draft via scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh) — wait for fa-extension.zip to appear on the release, then `gh run rerun <tag-run-id> --failed`. Root pattern: build-macos.yml build-extension derives "latest+1 at its own dispatch moment" and runs ~once daily, so any tag train landing after the daily leg has no fa-extension.zip and the gh-1832 gate correctly strands it as a draft (seen stuck: v1.0.637, v1.0.638 on 2026-10-24). "Advance vpinned marker" failing right after is downstream noise (pin_release.sh refuses to pin unsigned releases) — it self-heals once provenance lands. Note: gh run view --json jobs returns only the latest attempt; failed release-tail jobs may be absent from a stale ci-red ticket's job list if the report was filed before the tail finished. Also: a rerun --failed never resurrects SKIPPED jobs (e.g. Installer smoke) — benign, the Quality gate treats skipped as neutral. Systemic fix (follow-up gh-1847) LANDED the same day: the tag train builds fa-extension.zip itself (ci.yml build-extension, an additive continue-on-error leg mirroring web-spa; release-provenance needs it so the gh-1832 gate never races the attach), so a draft stranded on the missing zip now self-heals with a plain `gh run rerun <tag-run-id> --failed` — the manual producer dispatch above survives only as the fallback for a red or flaky extension leg, and the daily build-macos leg was kept as the next-tag-draft pre-stager.

---
id: "n_1010_828f"
type: "note"
title: "gh-1801 fix (2026-10-23): the release train's empty-latest-release creators were auto_release.sh (`gh release create --latest` with ZERO assets on every main-push train — the fa update 404 window) plus asset-less lazy creates in ci.yml binaries/web-spa and build-macos.yml CLI/extension jobs. Fixed by removing the auto_release create entirely (binaries job owns creation) and making every lazy create DRAFT-first with `--draft=false --latest` only in steps that upload a real fa-*.tar.gz/zip; release_attach_or_create.sh's attach path now publishes drafts too. # Note: n_1010_828f

gh-1801 fix (2026-10-23): the release train's empty-latest-release creators were auto_release.sh (`gh release create --latest` with ZERO assets on every main-push train — the fa update 404 window) plus asset-less lazy creates in ci.yml binaries/web-spa and build-macos.yml CLI/extension jobs. Fixed by removing the auto_release create entirely (binaries job owns creation) and making every lazy create DRAFT-first with `--draft=false --latest` only in steps that upload a real fa-*.tar.gz/zip; release_attach_or_create.sh's attach path now publishes drafts too. Invariant pinned by test/release_empty_latest_guard_test.dart (no release may become latest without a CLI asset). FORENSICS LESSON from the same ticket: the filed "mobile legs cancel each other via shared concurrency" was WRONG — build-mobile run 39905802767 was killed by its OWN 90m build-ios job ceiling (check-run annotation "exceeded the maximum execution time"), the sibling had finished 78 min earlier, and the #351 group is per-run_id with cancel-in-progress:false; ALSO the job declared runs-on [self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1] yet executed on fa-m5-2, so that runner carries a stale fa-m5-1 label in GitHub runner settings (repo code cannot fix; gh-1692 routing contract). Before blaming concurrency for a "cancelled" run: check the job's check-run annotations (timeout kills report conclusion=cancelled) and compare the sibling's completion time.

version's latest processed TestFlight build straight to App Store review (iOS and/or
macOS). Pre-flight fails before any mutation — version must exist (create it via
`store-metadata.yml`), a processed build must exist, an already-submitted version is a
green no-op — and `confirm` must repeat `version` exactly. Release-after-approval stays
a manual ASC click (`APP_STORE_AUTOMATIC_RELEASE` repo variable flips it).

`workflow_dispatch` input `legs` selects a single leg (`all` by default) —
the safe way to smoke one channel.

## Versioning

The scheme (gh-1522): the git TAG is the single source of truth —
`scripts/auto_release.sh` cuts an annotated tag (latest tag + 1) directly
on `origin/main` plus the GitHub Release, authenticated as the fa-release-bot
GitHub App (gh-1172 — its token triggers the tag-scoped jobs, which
`GITHUB_TOKEN` pushes never do). ZERO commits land on main: the retired
flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit (`pubspec.yaml`,
`CHANGELOG.md`, `flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}`) per release — noisy
history, a direct-to-main bot path, CHANGELOG growth toward the pub.dev
256 KiB cap (gh-1452) and pubspec.lock churn invalidating
`--enforce-lockfile` (gh-1265). Both pubspecs now carry the FIXED
`0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails the Static
`Version placeholder guard` — it would desync the tag↔staged-file
invariant), and CI stamps the real version at every edge:

- **pub.dev** — the `publish` job stages the package
  (`scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/publish-stage "${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"`)
  and the stage-time stamper (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`) writes the
  tag version into the staged pubspec, guards staged == tag pre-upload, and
  PREPENDS the tag's generated changelog section to the staged CHANGELOG
  (the repo file is never mutated). CHANGELOG.md in-repo is curated-only:
  PRs add lines under `## Unreleased`; `scripts/release_notes.sh` picks
  curated `## <version>` → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional
  commits since the previous tag. The pub.dev 262144-byte changelog cap is
  enforced on the STAGED file (oldest staged sections trim), so it can
  never block a release again — the publish job's repo-file check is
  ADVISORY (`::warning::` pointing at `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`), never a
  hard gate (gh-1522 rework, PR #1526).
- **App builds** — `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` derive
  `latest tag + 1` and pass it via `--build-name`/`--build-number`
  (BUILD_NUMBER = run number); the fastlane `store_pubspec_version` helper
  prefers the derived `BUILD_NAME` env.
- **Local / CLI** — `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe --tags`; `fa --version` reads the stamped `version.txt`
  first, the placeholder pubspec second (a plain `dart run` shows
  `0.0.0-dev` — self-explanatory).

Manual `workflow_dispatch` runs are input-gated: `releaseDryRun: true`
exercises the whole pipeline without the tag push (AC1), and
`releaseDispatch: true` on `refs/heads/main` is the real release — bare
validation dispatches (the SM's per-PR `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref
....
  the guard only deletes a draft whose body carries this very run+job's
  `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job> -->` marker — daily-publish
  runs the mobile and macOS legs concurrently on the same derived tag, and
  a failed leg's guard must never destroy the sibling leg's mid-upload
  draft (foreign or unmarked drafts are left to the sweeper). Pinned by
  `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` (a job with an asset-carrying create
  and no guard fails CI).
- **Attach-or-create** — the draft-capable creates of build-macos.yml /
  build-mobile.yml live in `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh`, which is

  in-flight draft), and the create stamps the ownership marker the guard
  verifies.
- **Daily sweeper** — the `sweep-drafts` job in `daily-publish.yml` runs

  and the marker is the only ownership proof — gh-2008; the bucket rule
  keys on the exact stamped shape, so prose merely mentioning the
  substring or a malformed marker stays human — review thread
  PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6yOzIh; id-based API
  delete, tag and git history untouched — draft assets are unpublished by
  definition, E2), human drafts (no marker) are listed but kept (E1),
  fresh (<24h) drafts are left for their in-flight run. The job grants
  `actions: read` — unmarked swept drafts name their creating run via
  `gh run list`, which 403s without it; marker drafts name the marker's
  run id directly. Anything
  stale files **one** deduplicated `release-hygiene` issue (comment on the
  open one, auto-close on a clean sweep — same convention as the leg
  issues) naming each swept draft and its creating run, so a recurring
  stuck draft points at its broken step. The test stub enforces the
  workflow-declared token permissions, so a dropped grant fails CI instead
  of silently degrading the issue to "no run on ref".
- **Naming** — titles are the bare `vX.Y.Z` tag everywhere (matches the

  titles (e.g. `Fa v0.1.362`) are deliberately not rewritten — backfill
  is opt-in per release.
- **Latest** — every publish path passes `--latest` explicitly (and

  release another path created first). Guards and the sweeper only ever

===
Closes #2008
### Root Cause
- Every pipeline release draft is created with `GH_TOKEN: secrets.RELEASE_PAT`, so GitHub attributes it to the PAT's owner (`@IstiN`, type `User`) — never a bot.
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh` classified stale drafts as bot-created only via `author.type == "Bot"` / `*[bot]` login and never read the body, so the release train's own orphaned drafts — each stamped `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job> -->` — were bucketed "human", kept forever (E1), and the sweep issue could never go clean. Verified on the live API: all 3 current drafts (incl. ticketed `v1.0.663`, `v1.0.665`) carry the marker.

### Fix
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh`: the inventory jq now also buckets a stale draft as pipeline-created when its body carries the `release-draft-owner` marker (the ownership signal `release_draft_guard.sh`/`release_draft_dedupe.sh` already parse), and names the marker's exact `run/<id>` in the filed issue (more accurate than the tag-ref `gh run list` fallback — the creating run executed on main). Unmarked human drafts stay listed-not-deleted (E1); fresh marker drafts stay untouched.
- `docs/ci.md`: sweeper paragraph updated to the new classification.

### Test Coverage
- `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` AC2 (new): stale marker draft with human author is DELETED and the issue names `actions/runs/40822965933`; stale unmarked human draft kept; fresh marker draft untouched — failed before the fix, passes after.
- Owning suite `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`: 53 passed. Release/CI-hygiene neighborhood (10 suites): 289 passed. Full `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **13208 passed, 13 skipped (pre-existing), 0 failed**.

### Notes
- No workflow/permission changes; `actions:read` is still needed for the unmarked-bot-draft run lookup.
- `v1.0.663`/`v1.0.665` are live orphans of dead runs — the next daily sweep with this fix deletes them and auto-closes this issue.
- Commit: `d29841a` on `ai/gh-2008`.

So my job for gh-2026: root-cause why the drafts went stale and fix the actual lifecycle hole.

Here's an example: ``` on: release: types: [published] jobs: release: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: Filter release event id: filter-release run: \| tag_name="${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}" if [[ "$tag_name" =~ ^@rightcapital/.* ]]; then echo "Matched tag name: $tag_name" exit 0 else echo "Tag name does not match: $tag_name" exit 1 fi - name: Publish release uses: actions/create-release@v6 if: steps.filter-release.outputs.status == 0 ``` In this example, the filter-release step uses a shell script to check if the tag name starts with @rightcapital/. If it does, it exits with a status code of 0, which means that the publish-release step will run. If the tag name doesn't match, it exits with a status code of 1, which means that the publish-release step will not run. |

=== release-mobile checkout ===

      - name: Download store APK artifact
        if: needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: android-apk-store
          path: artifacts/

      - name: Download god APK artifact
        if: needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: android-apk-god
          path: artifacts/

      - name: List downloaded artifacts
        if: needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
        run: ls -laR artifacts/

      - name: Create or update GitHub Release
        if: needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # PAT (not the job token) so the tag push fires tag CI — the
          # attach-or-create script builds its push URL only when GH_TOKEN
          # is set; without it `git push ""` died with "fatal: bad
          # repository ''" (2026-10-22 v1.0.626 mobile leg).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

No `persist-credentials: false` anywhere — every checkout in build-mobile.yml (there's one at the top of the workflow, let me verify) persists the GITHUB_TOKEN extraheader into the local git config for all later steps. 2. release_attach_or_create.sh pushes `git push https://x-access-token:<RELEASE_PAT>@github.com/...` — the URL userinfo loses to the extraheader Authorization (documented Actions gotcha; both headers are computed but the server sees the checkout's GITHUB_TOKEN basic auth as the effective credential).

content.text:
# auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      (github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true)) &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (schedule, releaseDispatch — gh-1537 retired the main-push
      # trigger, so there is no push arm) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push, nothing else. gh-1801: auto_release.sh no longer
          # creates the GitHub Release (an asset-less create publishes an
          # empty `latest`) — the tag-run binaries job owns creation.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh-1801 (rework): no GH_TOKEN is exported here anymore —
          # auto_release.sh no longer calls `gh` at all (the asset-less
          # create published an empty `latest` and broke `fa update`; the
          # binaries job owns creation, draft-first). The tag push rides
          # the checkout App token above (gh-1172).
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).
  #
  # gh-1280: merge-blocking validations ride `workflow_dispatch` (Machine SM
  # dispatches this workflow on the PR head; the dispatched run registers its
  # check runs on the head SHA), while this gate fired only on `pull_request`
  # events. Every real validation run therefore skipped the matrix and the
  # required "Binaries smoke gate" context went green-by-skip — a broken arch
  # build (the v1.0.512 linux/arm64 class) could never block a merge. On a
  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

  binaries-pr:
    name: Binaries (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')

ci.yml's release job (auto_release tag push):
```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@...

   fetch-depth: 0
   filter: blob:none
   # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
   # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
   # trigger downstream workflow runs.
   token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
``

**actions/checkout with `token: <App token>`** → the persisted extraheader carries the APP token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) → the push (plain `git push` with NO URL credentials — auto_release.sh pushes `origin`) authenticates as the App → triggers CI. 

So the repo's canonical answer to "how does a workflow push a tag that triggers CI": **pass a non-GITHUB_TOKEN into actions/checkout's `token` input so the persisted extraheader credentials ARE the triggering token.** The auto_release path does exactly this and works daily.

The daily legs' release_attach_or_create path instead relies on URL-embedded RELEASE_PAT creds — which lose to the checkout's persisted GITHUB_TOKEN extraheader. This nails the root cause with in-repo evidence:

- auto_release: App token via checkout `token:` → extraheader = App token → tag CI fires. ✓ (every tag 625–677 except 663/65)

**Variant 1 (mirror the auto_release idiom)**: in release-macos/release-mobile jobs, pass `token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}` to actions/checkout → the persisted extraheader becomes the PAT → `git push` (even a bare `git push origin` or the URL form) authenticates as the PAT → triggers CI. So the lazy draft's missing-ref case can only fire where the PAT exists.

Hmm — wait, now that I think about it — is Fix C (lazy draft mint) REALLY needed for THIS ticket? Let me reconsider scope discipline once more. The ticket: two stale drafts from GREEN runs; root cause: mint push suppressed the train. If I fix A+B only:

- The 663/65 scenario (mobile leg mints) → fixed: push fires train; if not, guard fails the job + deletes draft.
- The sibling scenario (build-macos-cli/build-extension lazy-create mints silently for a missing ref) → NOT fixed: the tag exists silently, all attach legs skip their push, draft rots → SWEEP ISSUE AGAIN (recurrence!). The ticket explicitly says "Recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing". This path produces EXACTLY the same un-owned stale draft, and the repo already documents it as a defect class (issue #597) it fixed for attach-or-create but never for lazy-draft. # Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Daily release legs (build-mobile) left release drafts `v1.0.663` / `v1.0.665` unpublished; the daily sweeper deleted both and filed the recurring sweep issue (gh-2026, after gh-2008/#2010 had already filed and "handled" the same two drafts once).

**Root cause**: The draft-creating runs were GREEN — the draft was orphaned by a **credential-precedence bug in the annotated-tag mint that silently suppresses the tag CI train**:

1. On a quiet-main morning the `release-mobile` job was the first leg to touch the derived tag. `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh` found the tag DEFINITELY missing (`git ls-remote --exit-code` rc 2), minted the annotated tag and pushed it: `git push https://x-access-token:<RELEASE_PAT>@github.com/...` (log: "tag v1.0.663 missing — creating annotated tag … (PAT push, fires tag CI)"), then created the ownership-marked draft with 3 mobile assets. Run 40822965933 at 2026-10-29T05:35:17Z, run 40868152070 at 12:18:14Z. Both jobs concluded **success**.
2. The push never authenticated as the PAT. `actions/checkout` (persist-credentials defaults true; no `persist-credentials: false` anywhere in the workflows) persists the **job token** in the repo-local git config as `http.https://github.com/.extraheader = AUTHORIZATION: basic <GITHUB_TOKEN>`. That header is appended to every git HTTP request to github.com and **outranks the URL-embedded credentials on the wire**, so GitHub attributed the push to the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
3. GitHub **never fires workflow runs for pushes made with the repository's GITHUB_TOKEN** (docs "Triggering a workflow from a workflow"; the repo's own docs/ci.md and the ci.yml release job comment say the same: the tag push must ride a non-GITHUB_TOKEN checkout token "so the pushed tag triggers the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs"). Result: **zero workflow runs ever existed on `refs/tags/v1.0.663` / `v1.0.665`** (verified: `?branch=<tag>` run list = 0; the commits' check-suites contain no suite with those head_branches), so `ci.yml`'s binaries/web-spa/build-extension/release-provenance never ran and the draft — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801) — had no publish path.
4. Nothing else could catch it: the leg was green so the failure-path draft guard (`if: always() && job.status != 'success'`) never fired; the mint path has **no verification that the pushed tag actually started the train** — that is the missing lifecycle guard. The draft rotted until the sweeper deleted it (gh-2008's marker rule made them deletable → issue #2026).

Evidence that the override is systematic, not a GitHub incident:
- Every v* tag cut by the ci.yml release job fired its tag CI within seconds (v1.0.625–v1.0.677 — that job pushes via `actions/checkout` with `token: <fa-release-bot App token>`, i.e. the persisted extraheader IS a triggering token).
- 100% of the mint-path pushes since the push URL was introduced (PR #1783, 2026-10-22) fired **no** CI: v1.0.663 and v1.0.665 are the only two mints ever attempted (every other day the legs attached to releases the auto-release train had already created), and both produced orphaned drafts.
- The REST API calls in the same steps (release create) DID attribute to the PAT's owner (@IstiN — gh-2008 RCA), proving the PAT itself was valid and present; only the git push lost it to the header.

**Impact**: Every time a daily leg mints a NEW tag (quiet main — the daily runs before any auto-release coalesce), the release draft is stranded: the train never starts, the leg is green, and the draft is swept ~24h later, re-filing the sweep issue. Assets (AAB/APKs/DMGs/IPA) upload fine; the release simply never publishes. Secondary effect: the swept tags remain as annotated refs, so the next auto-release derives its "latest tag + 1" past them (no version gap, but no train ever ran for the swept versions).

**Fix approach**:
- `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh`: before the mint push, strip the persisted checkout extraheader(s) (`http.<host>/.extraheader`) from the local git config — exactly what the Actions runner's own post-job cleanup does — so the URL's PAT credentials are what GitHub sees and the push fires the tag train.
- Lifecycle guard (the missing one): after the mint push, verify the train actually started — bounded poll for any workflow run on the tag ref (`gh run list --branch <tag>`); on absence fail the step with a self-explaining `::error::` so the job's existing ownership-scoped draft guard reclaims the draft immediately instead of rotting it for a day.
- Same defect class closed where it lives next: `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh` lets `gh release create --draft` REST-mint the tag when the ref is missing — a lightweight tag with **no push event at all** (the documented v0.1.408 silent class, issue #597) — which strands the same drafts when the fast extension/CLI legs beat the attach legs. It now mints through the same annotated-push helper.
- Requires `actions: read` on the `release-macos` / `release-mobile` jobs for the run-list probe (same grant rationale the sweeper already carries, review of #294).

**Previous attempt**: PR #2010 (gh-2008) fixed only the sweeper's classification (marker-stamped drafts authored by the human PAT are pipeline-created, so they get deleted instead of kept forever). Its RCA ("live orphans of dead runs") was wrong — the creating runs were green, not dead — so the underlying suppression was never fixed and the sweep issue recurred one day later (this ticket).

python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
for p, fn in [('test/release_attach_or_create_mint_test.dart','_runMint'), ('test/release_lazy_draft_mint_test.dart','_runLazyMint')]:
    s = open(p).read()
    # Replace record-pattern destructurings with a plain result variable.
    s = re.sub(r'final \(:exitCode, :output, :capturedPushLines, :gitLogLines\) =\s*\n\s*'+fn+r'\(',
               'final r = '+fn+'(', s)
    s = re.sub(r'final \(:exitCode, :output, :ghLogLines, :capturedPushLines, :gitLogLines\) =\s*\n\s*'+fn+r'\(',
               'final r = '+fn+'(', s)
    s = re.sub(r'final \(:exitCode, :output, :ghLogLines, :capturedPushLines\) =\s*\n\s*'+fn+r'\(',
               'final r = '+fn+'(', s)
    s = re.sub(r'final \(:exitCode, :output, :ghLogLines, :gitLogLines\) =\s*\n\s*'+fn+r'\(',
               'final r = '+fn+'(', s)
    s = re.sub(r'final \(:exitCode, :output, :capturedPushLines\) =\s*\n\s*'+fn+r'\(',
               'final r = '+fn+'(', s)
    # Fix field references inside test bodies (only within expect/variable uses).
    s = s.replace('expect(exitCode,', 'expect(r.exitCode,')
    s = s.replace('expect(output,', 'expect(r.output,')
    s = s.replace('expect(capturedPushLines,', 'expect(r.capturedPushLines,')
    s = s.replace('expect(ghLogLines,', 'expect(r.ghLogLines,')
    s = s.replace('capturedPushLines.single', 'r.capturedPushLines.single')
    s = s.replace('ghLogLines.where', 'r.ghLogLines.where')
    s = s.replace('ghLogLines.any', 'r.ghLogLines.any')
    s = s.replace('gitLogLines.indexWhere', 'r.gitLogLines.indexWhere')
    s = s.replace('gitLogLines.any', 'r.gitLogLines.any')
    s = s.replace('r.output.contains(', 'r.output.contains(')
    s = s.replace('reason: output)', 'reason: r.output)')
    s = s.replace("'(gh log: $ghLogLines)'", "'(gh log: ${r.ghLogLines})'")
    s = s.replace("'(git log: '\n            '$gitLogLines)'", "'(git log: ${r.gitLogLines})'")
    s = s.replace('$gitLogLines)', '${r.gitLogLines})')
    s = s.replace('$ghLogLines)', '${r.ghLogLines})')
    open(p,'w').write(s)
print('rewritten')
EOF
